lines: Saws are off the wall and in the ice, and I have not looked at the wall once since.
Three times this month they came down and went back up. It was the fourth time that counted.
My hands have stopped doing that thing. I never told anybody they were doing it.
The saws are down off the wall, oiled, and back up on the wall again.
Third time this month. There is nothing else to do with my hands and they know it.
Six names on six saws, and the top one is worn down to two letters.
You are given one at eleven and you file your own name into the tang. It takes a week.
Do it badly and you live with it. Mine has a crooked R and I am fifty-eight.
I filed my name in on Tuesday. You do it the winter you first cut, and I cut.
Six generations, and mine is the shortest name on the beam and the deepest one in it.
My father did not say anything. He went and stood outside for a while.
I have not filed my name in yet. You do it the winter you first cut.
Nobody has said anything about that. Everybody in this house has thought about it.
Mine is the short one, third from the bottom. It is not sharp, and that is on purpose.
Dad says a sharp saw in a soft hand takes the hand. So I get a blunt one for a year.
